items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.description: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. This task is difficult when it requires specialist linguistic or scientific knowledge. We used the Wikipedia Game to test language models on an analogous information retrieval task. In the game, players must reach a target article using only article links. We compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across five Wikipedia languages and five academic-literature datasets. items.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
items.description: Interpreting machine learning model predictions is a central challenge, particularly for black-box vision models. Concept-based attribution methods interpret models using human-understandable concepts. Existing concept-based methods can only interpret classification and regression models. They require access to model weights or large concept-annotated datasets, and most methods cannot provide image-level attribution. items.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks

items.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Deep-space communications operate under intermittent connectivity, long propagation delays, and relay storage constraints. In such networks, the Bundle Protocol enables store-carry-forward communication, requiring relay nodes to manage limited storage and scarce contact opportunities. items.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.description: Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. items.name: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
items.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
items.description: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. items.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
items.description: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly analyze and reason about images, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations faithfully encode the structured relations required for such reasoning. items.title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
items.description: While deep learning models for tabular data have recently received significant research attention, the choice of objective functions for regression tasks remains an understudied degree of freedom. items.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
items.description: Neural semantic parsers generate meaning representations token by token, yet well-formedness depends on references, scope, and graph relations that unfold during generation. Constrained decoding prevents locally invalid tokens but does not guarantee that a valid prefix can be completed within a fixed output-length limit. items.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
items.description: Large language models reuse the same attention heads across tasks, but identifying these shared heads does not explain what they do differently in each task. A natural source of inspiration is task-dependent interactions among shared brain regions, which motivate a network view of language-model computation. items.name: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.description: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. items.name: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.description: Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools. As the effects of their actions accumulate and interact across services, unintended or harmful outcomes can arise when agents fulfill benign user requests. Proactively identifying these compositional failures requires systematically exploring diverse cross-service paths. items.title: Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design
items.description: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. items.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents

items.name: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
items.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
items.description: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. items.title: Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency
items.description: An ideal (language) model must continually update its knowledge. Existing work largely focuses on making these updates efficient after training. We investigate how the organization of time-varying knowledge during pre-training shapes the efficiency of subsequent updates. items.title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) promise to bring the benefits of continuous flow modelling to language, including accelerated sampling and controllable generation. The field has grown rapidly, and the capabilities of CDLMs have begun to rival those of discrete diffusion. items.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
items.description: When solving complex spatial reasoning tasks, ordinary humans naturally revisit the scenes from task-relevant viewpoints and mentally reconstruct the spatial layouts from those viewpoints. But can Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) proactively think in the same way? items.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
items.description: Recent advances in automatic pronunciation assessment (APA) have driven a shift from scripted to free-form assessment. items.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
items.description: A useful language model should know when to answer and when to say "I don't know."
